title: Stay-at-home fathers“
titleChinese: 全职奶爸”不再是非主流
paragraphs: There aren’t many parents who would say that raising children is easy. For many people, having children can force parents to choose between career and family. Sometimes it comes down to finances – sending a child to nursery or hiring a nanny can be a huge financial burden that is unsustainable, while others may feel it’s better to be a hands-on parent. These days, more and more men are choosing to stay at home to look after their offspring. So why are more dads opting to put their careers on hold, and what does the job entail?

With more women working outside the home than 70 years ago, if the need is there for one parent to stay at home, it could simply come down to who earns more – the biggest breadwinner. And with attitudes changing towards a man’s role in the family, it seems to be easier for them to enter full-time parenthood. Sadly, though, men may still face stigmas by choosing to raise their child. A 2013 study in the US by the Pews Research Center found that 51% of people thought children were better off if a mother is home and doesn’t have a job, while 8% say the same about a father. But what do parents have to do when they choose to stay with their kids?

In the early stages, a baby is totally dependent on a carer. The changing of nappies, burping after milk and making sure they feed on time are just some of the vital 24-7 activities an infant relies on. During this period, many parents take paternity and maternity leave from work. But as a child gets older, it can become less about necessity and more about choice. Rather than opt for a creche, which can prove expensive, either parent may remain at home to educate, protect and play with their child to help them develop and grow.

It’s a difficult job, with a demanding ‘boss’, but it can also be incredibly rewarding for those willing to do it. And with attitudes changing towards who should stay at home, maybe more and more fathers will choose to become stay-at-home dads.

vocabulary.entry: come down to /kʌm daʊn tuː/ 归结为；归根结底是
vocabulary.example: The success of the project comes down to teamwork and dedication.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目的成功归根结底是团队合作和奉献精神的结果。

vocabulary.entry: nursery /ˈnɜːsəri/ n. 托儿所；保育院
vocabulary.example: She sends her two-year-old son to a local nursery every weekday.
vocabulary.translation: 她每个工作日都把两岁的儿子送到当地的托儿所。

vocabulary.entry: nanny /ˈnæni/ n. 保姆；育婴师
vocabulary.example: The family hired a nanny to take care of their newborn baby.
vocabulary.translation: 这家人雇了一位保姆来照顾他们的新生儿。

vocabulary.entry: financial burden /faɪˈnænʃl ˈbɜːdn/ 经济负担
vocabulary.example: Paying for medical treatment has become a heavy financial burden for the family.
vocabulary.translation: 支付医疗费用成了这个家庭沉重的经济负担。

vocabulary.entry: unsustainable /ˌʌnsəˈsteɪnəbl/ adj. 无法持续的；难以为继的
vocabulary.example: The company's current business model is unsustainable in the long term.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司目前的商业模式长期来看是难以为继的。

vocabulary.entry: hands-on /ˌhændz ˈɒn/ adj. 亲力亲为的；实际操作的
vocabulary.example: He is a hands-on parent who always participates in his children's school activities.
vocabulary.translation: 他是个亲力亲为的家长，总是参与孩子们的校园活动。

vocabulary.entry: offspring /ˈɒfsprɪŋ/ n. 子女；后代
vocabulary.example: The bird feeds its offspring with insects it catches in the forest.
vocabulary.translation: 这只鸟用在森林里捕捉的昆虫喂养自己的幼鸟。

vocabulary.entry: put...on hold /pʊt ɒn həʊld/ 搁置；暂停
vocabulary.example: She decided to put her career on hold to look after her sick mother.
vocabulary.translation: 她决定搁置自己的事业，去照顾生病的母亲。

vocabulary.entry: entail /ɪnˈteɪl/ v. 牵涉；需要；使必要
vocabulary.example: The job entails working abroad for six months every year.
vocabulary.translation: 这份工作需要每年在国外工作六个月。

vocabulary.entry: breadwinner /ˈbredwɪnə(r)/ n. 养家糊口的人
vocabulary.example: After his father retired, he became the main breadwinner of the family.
vocabulary.translation: 父亲退休后，他成了家里的主要经济支柱。

vocabulary.entry: full-time parenthood /ˌfʊl taɪm ˈpeərənhʊd/ 全职育儿
vocabulary.example: More and more people are choosing full-time parenthood to accompany their children's growth.
vocabulary.translation: 越来越多的人选择全职育儿，陪伴孩子成长。

vocabulary.entry: stigma /ˈstɪɡmə/ n. 污名；耻辱
vocabulary.example: There is still a social stigma attached to mental health problems in some areas.
vocabulary.translation: 在一些地区，心理健康问题仍然带有社会污名。

vocabulary.entry: dependent on /dɪˈpendənt ɒn/ 依赖；依靠
vocabulary.example: Young children are completely dependent on their parents for food and shelter.
vocabulary.translation: 幼儿在衣食住行上完全依赖父母。

vocabulary.entry: carer /ˈkeərə(r)/ n. 照料者；护理人员
vocabulary.example: The elderly woman has a dedicated carer who visits her every day.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老年妇女有一位敬业的护理人员，每天都会来照顾她。

vocabulary.entry: nappy /ˈnæpi/ n. 尿布
vocabulary.example: She changed the baby's dirty nappy and then gave him a bottle of milk.
vocabulary.translation: 她给宝宝换了脏尿布，然后喂了他一瓶奶。

vocabulary.entry: burp /bɜːp/ v. 使打嗝；拍嗝
vocabulary.example: The mother gently patted the baby's back to burp him after feeding.
vocabulary.translation: 喂完奶后，妈妈轻轻拍着宝宝的后背帮他拍嗝。

vocabulary.entry: 24-7 /ˌtwenti ˈfɔː ˈsevən/ 全天候的；昼夜不停的
vocabulary.example: The emergency hotline provides 24-7 service for people in need.
vocabulary.translation: 这条紧急热线为有需要的人提供全天候服务。

vocabulary.entry: paternity leave /pəˈtɜːnəti liːv/ 陪产假
vocabulary.example: The company offers two weeks of paid paternity leave for new fathers.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司为新晋爸爸提供两周的带薪陪产假。

vocabulary.entry: maternity leave /məˈtɜːnəti liːv/ 产假
vocabulary.example: She took six months of maternity leave after giving birth to her daughter.
vocabulary.translation: 生下女儿后，她休了六个月的产假。

vocabulary.entry: creche /kreʃ/ n. 托儿所；日托中心
vocabulary.example: The office has an on-site creche for employees with young children.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司设有内部托儿所，方便有小孩的员工。

vocabulary.entry: demanding /dɪˈmɑːndɪŋ/ adj. 要求高的；费力的
vocabulary.example: Being a teacher is a rewarding but demanding job.
vocabulary.translation: 当老师是一份有意义但要求很高的工作。

vocabulary.entry: rewarding /rɪˈwɔːdɪŋ/ adj. 有意义的；值得做的
vocabulary.example: Volunteering at the community center is a very rewarding experience.
vocabulary.translation: 在社区中心做志愿者是一段非常有意义的经历。

vocabulary.entry: stay-at-home dad /ˌsteɪ æt həʊm ˈdæd/ 全职爸爸
vocabulary.example: He used to be a manager in a company, but now he is a happy stay-at-home dad.
vocabulary.translation: 他以前是一家公司的经理，现在是一位快乐的全职爸爸。

vocabulary.entry: vital /ˈvaɪtl/ adj. 至关重要的；必不可少的
vocabulary.example: A balanced diet is vital for maintaining good health.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡的饮食对保持身体健康至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: develop /dɪˈveləp/ v. 成长；发育；发展
vocabulary.example: Playing with other children helps kids develop their social skills.
vocabulary.translation: 和其他孩子一起玩耍有助于培养孩子的社交能力。

vocabulary.entry: attitude /ˈætɪtjuːd/ n. 态度；看法
vocabulary.example: People's attitude towards gender roles has changed a lot over the years.
vocabulary.translation: 这些年来，人们对性别角色的看法发生了很大变化。

sentences.english: There aren’t many parents who would say that raising children is easy.
sentences.chinese: 没多少父母会说养育孩子是件容易的事。

sentences.english: For many people, having children can force parents to choose between career and family.
sentences.chinese: 对很多人而言，有了孩子之后，父母往往要在事业和家庭之间做出抉择。

sentences.english: Sometimes it comes down to finances – sending a child to nursery or hiring a nanny can be a huge financial burden that is unsustainable, while others may feel it’s better to be a hands-on parent.
sentences.chinese: 有时候，这归根结底是经济问题——送孩子去托儿所或是雇保姆，可能会成为难以承受的巨大经济负担；而另一些父母则认为，亲历亲为照顾孩子会更好。

sentences.english: These days, more and more men are choosing to stay at home to look after their offspring.
sentences.chinese: 如今，越来越多的男性选择留在家中照顾子女。

sentences.english: So why are more dads opting to put their careers on hold, and what does the job entail?
sentences.chinese: 那么，为什么越来越多的父亲愿意搁置自己的事业？这份“工作”又需要承担哪些职责呢？

sentences.english: With more women working outside the home than 70 years ago, if the need is there for one parent to stay at home, it could simply come down to who earns more – the biggest breadwinner.
sentences.chinese: 与70年前相比，如今有更多女性外出工作。如果家庭需要父母中的一方留在家中，那么这件事很简单，就看谁的收入更高——谁是家里主要的经济支柱。

sentences.english: And with attitudes changing towards a man’s role in the family, it seems to be easier for them to enter full-time parenthood.
sentences.chinese: 随着人们对男性在家庭中角色的看法逐渐转变，男性成为全职家长也变得更容易被接受。

sentences.english: Sadly, though, men may still face stigmas by choosing to raise their child.
sentences.chinese: 但遗憾的是，选择亲自抚养孩子的男性仍可能面临偏见。

sentences.english: A 2013 study in the US by the Pews Research Center found that 51% of people thought children were better off if a mother is home and doesn’t have a job, while 8% say the same about a father.
sentences.chinese: 皮尤研究中心2013年在美国开展的一项研究显示，51%的人认为，如果母亲不上班、留在家中，孩子会过得更好；而只有8%的人认为父亲留在家中也能达到同样的效果。

sentences.english: But what do parents have to do when they choose to stay with their kids?
sentences.chinese: 那么，选择留在家中陪伴孩子的父母，具体需要做些什么呢？

sentences.english: In the early stages, a baby is totally dependent on a carer.
sentences.chinese: 在孩子很小的时候，婴儿完全依赖照顾者的照料。

sentences.english: The changing of nappies, burping after milk and making sure they feed on time are just some of the vital 24-7 activities an infant relies on.
sentences.chinese: 换尿布、喂完奶后拍嗝、确保孩子按时进食，这些只是婴儿所需的全天候重要照料工作中的一部分。

sentences.english: During this period, many parents take paternity and maternity leave from work.
sentences.chinese: 在这个阶段，许多父母会申请育儿假。

sentences.english: But as a child gets older, it can become less about necessity and more about choice.
sentences.chinese: 但随着孩子逐渐长大，父母留在家中就不再是出于必需，而更多是一种选择。

sentences.english: Rather than opt for a creche, which can prove expensive, either parent may remain at home to educate, protect and play with their child to help them develop and grow.
sentences.chinese: 由于托儿所的费用可能十分高昂，父母中的任何一方都可能选择留在家中，通过教育、保护和陪伴孩子玩耍，帮助孩子健康成长。

sentences.english: It’s a difficult job, with a demanding ‘boss’, but it can also be incredibly rewarding for those willing to do it.
sentences.chinese: 这是一份艰巨的工作，面对的是一位“要求苛刻的老板”，但对于愿意承担这份工作的人来说，它也能带来难以言喻的成就感。

sentences.english: And with attitudes changing towards who should stay at home, maybe more and more fathers will choose to become stay-at-home dads.
sentences.chinese: 随着人们对于谁该留在家中这一问题的看法不断转变，或许会有越来越多的父亲选择成为全职爸爸。
